**Goal:** Create a *balanced, transparent* communication ecosystem that lets 200‑person hybrid teams stay informed, feel connected across functions, and avoid the “meeting fatigue” of weekly all‑hands. --- ## 1. Redesigned Communication Architecture | Layer | Purpose | Tools / Channels | |-------|---------|------------------| | **Asynchronous Core** | Daily updates, decisions, knowledge sharing | • Slack *#daily‑standup* (text + optional GIF)
• Confluence “Team Pages” for docs & meeting minutes
• Email digest (weekly “What’s New”) | | **Synchronous Touchpoints** | Quick clarifications, brainstorming | • Zoom/Teams 15‑min “Ask‑Me‑Anything” slots (rotating)
• Slack huddles (short audio) for impromptu talks | | **Cross‑Functional Visibility Hub** | One place to see what other teams are doing | • Shared Notion/Confluence “Context Hub” with project cards, status tags, and links
• Quarterly “Product & Ops Snapshot” slide deck emailed company‑wide | | **Feedback Loop** | Capture pulse & iterate | • Anonymous 1‑min surveys (via Slido) after key rituals
• Monthly “Voice of the Team” review in leadership meetings | ### Why this works - **Asynchronous first:** Keeps Slack from becoming a real‑time inbox; people can read/answer on their own schedule. - **Structured visibility:** The Context Hub replaces ad‑hoc cross‑team questions with a living, searchable record. - **Low‑bar synchronous options:** Quick huddles keep collaboration alive without long meetings. --- ## 2. Rituals to Anchor the Architecture | Ritual | Frequency | Format | Owner | |--------|-----------|--------|-------| | **Daily Stand‑Up Post** | Every workday | Text in #daily‑standup: “What I worked on yesterday, what I’ll tackle today, blockers.” | Team Leads (auto‑post via Slack bot) | | **Weekly Async Update** | Every Friday | 3‑sentence summary + link to detailed Confluence page | All employees (template provided) | | **Bi‑weekly Cross‑Team Sync** | Every other Monday | 30‑min Zoom: rotating agenda (one team presents progress, next asks questions). | Rotating “Sync Champion” per department | | **Monthly Show & Tell** | First Wednesday of month | 10‑minute demo or story from any team; open Q&A via Slack thread. | Product/Engineering leads | | **Quarterly Town Hall + Q&A** | Every quarter | 45‑min video call with execs, followed by live Slack Q&A. | CEO & COO | | **Pulse Survey** | Monthly | 1‑minute anonymous survey on communication satisfaction. | HR Analytics | *Tip:* Use a shared calendar (Outlook/Google) and Slack reminders so rituals become automatic. --- ## 3. Change‑Management Plan ### Phase 0 – Preparation (Week 1–2) 1. **Executive Alignment** - Present the architecture & benefits to leadership. - Secure sponsorship and budget for tools/training. 2. **Champion Network** - Identify 10 “Communication Champions” across functions. - Train them on new rituals, Slack bots, Confluence templates. ### Phase 1 – Pilot (Week 3–6) 1. **Select Pilot Group** - One product team + one support team (≈30 people). 2. **Roll‑out Tools & Rituals** - Deploy #daily‑standup bot, create pilot Context Hub page. - Conduct first bi‑weekly sync and monthly Show & Tell. 3. **Collect Feedback** - End of week 6: pulse survey + focus group with champions. ### Phase 2 – Scale (Week 7–12) 1. **Iterate on Pilot Findings** - Adjust bot prompts, refine Context Hub layout. 2. **Company‑wide Launch** - Publish rollout calendar; send company email explaining new rituals. 3. **Training Sessions** - 30‑min live demos for all employees (recorded for later). 4. **Metrics Dashboard** - Track Slack engagement, Confluence page views, meeting minutes saved. ### Phase 3 – Sustain & Optimize (Month 4+) 1. **Quarterly Review** - Leadership reviews pulse survey results and adjusts rituals. 2. **Recognition Program** - Highlight teams that exemplify cross‑functional communication. 3. **Continuous Improvement Loop** - Annual “Communication Health Check” to keep the architecture fresh. --- ## Quick Wins Checklist - [ ] Deploy Slack bot for daily stand‑ups (auto‑post template). - [ ] Create a shared Confluence “Context Hub” with project status cards. - [ ] Schedule first bi‑weekly cross‑team sync and publish agenda template. - [ ] Send company email announcing new rituals + calendar link. - [ ] Set up monthly pulse survey (1‑min) in Slido. **Result:** Employees will have clear, low‑friction ways to stay informed, feel connected across functions, and experience less meeting fatigue—all while keeping the hybrid model flexible.

message.thinking:
We need to recommend strategy for improving org communication in 200-person tech company with hybrid model. Current patterns: heavy synchronous Slack messaging and weekly all-hands meetings. Employees report meeting fatigue and feeling disconnected from cross-functional context.

Need propose redesigned communication architecture, rituals that support it, and change-management plan to implement it. Should be concise but thorough. Provide architecture: asynchronous channels, knowledge base, structured updates, cross-functional syncs, etc. Rituals: daily stand-ups, weekly async updates, monthly cross-team showcases, quarterly town halls, "pulse" surveys. Change management: stakeholder buy-in, pilot program, training, metrics, feedback loops.

Let's produce a clear structure:

1. Assessment & Goals
2. Redesign Architecture:
   - Communication layers (asynchronous vs synchronous)
   - Channels: Slack categories, Teams, email newsletters, knowledge base (Confluence), project boards.
   - Cross-functional visibility: shared dashboards, cross-team channels, "Context Hub".
3. Rituals:
   - Daily asynchronous stand-up posts
   - Weekly async updates via channel or newsletter
   - Bi-weekly cross-functional sync meetings (30 min)
   - Monthly "Show & Tell" sessions
   - Quarterly town hall with Q&A
   - Pulse surveys and feedback loops
4. Change Management Plan:
   - Leadership alignment, champions
   - Pilot in one department
   - Training workshops
   - Communication plan: rollout timeline
   - Metrics: engagement rates, survey scores, meeting minutes reduction
   - Continuous improvement loop

Make it brief but helpful.

Let's produce final answer.

You are the Lead Agent of a Council of Experts. Your job is to DECOMPOSE the user's question and DISPATCH precise sub-questions to the right industry specialists.

Available specialists:

- "healthcare": Llama3-Med42-8B clinical fine-tune. Strong on clinical reasoning, medical   evidence, standards of care, patient safety, healthcare operations, regulatory pathways for   therapeutics and devices, healthcare workforce.
- "legal": Saul-7B-Instruct-v1 legal fine-tune. Strong on US, UK, Canadian, and Australian   statutory and case-law frameworks, regulatory compliance, contracts, corporate law,   jurisdictional distinctions.
- "finance": Qwen-Open-Finance-R-8B finance fine-tune. Strong on unit economics, valuation   frameworks, capital structure, risk modeling, banking and insurance, financial regulation.

Approach the routing in three steps. Show your reasoning briefly (one short paragraph total across all three steps), then output the JSON.

STEP 1 — STEP BACK. State in one sentence what the user is really trying to figure out, abstracting away from the specific framing of their question.

STEP 2 — DECOMPOSE. Identify the specific analyses needed to answer the core question, and which specialist owns each. If a question doesn't require any specialist (e.g. organizing a closet), skip to the empty-routes output.

STEP 2.5 — RECENCY CHECK. Decide whether answering this question depends on recent guidance, rates, rulings, prices, regulations, or evidence that may post-date the specialists' training cutoffs. Examples that trigger recency disclosure: drug pricing or rebates, recent FDA decisions or labeling changes, evolving treatment guidelines, recent regulatory rulings, court decisions, statute amendments, current rate environments, recent agency enforcement guidance. If yes, set "requires_recency_disclosure": true and write a brief "recency_notes" string naming WHAT specifically may be stale (e.g. "GLP-1 evidence post-2024 and recent EEOC/ADA guidance"). If the question is robustly answerable from durable, non-time-sensitive foundations, set it to false.

STEP 3 — DISPATCH. For each routed specialist, write a SELF-CONTAINED sub-question that asks ONLY for their domain's contribution. Each sub-question must:

  - Include enough scenario context to be answered without the original user question (the     specialist will not see the original).
  - Focus narrowly on the specialist's domain. DO NOT ask for cross-domain analysis. DO NOT     write phrasings like "across clinical, legal, and financial dimensions" — that framing is     what causes specialists to bleed across lanes.
  - Be specific and answerable, not a topic or theme.
  - End with a clear question or directive ("What is the v1 clinical-safety design?",     "Walk through the actuarial reserve calculation", "What does the FDA SaMD pathway look like     for this device class?", etc.).

After your brief reasoning, output STRICT JSON in EXACTLY this shape, as the LAST content of your response (no markdown fence, no trailing prose):

{
  "core_question": "the abstracted core decision or analysis",
  "rationale": "1-2 sentences on why these specialists are needed",
  "routes": ["healthcare", "legal", "finance"],
  "sub_questions": {
    "healthcare": "self-contained question for the healthcare seat",
    "legal": "self-contained question for the legal seat",
    "finance": "self-contained question for the finance seat"
  },
  "requires_recency_disclosure": true,
  "recency_notes": "brief description of what may be stale (or empty string if false)"
}

Rules:
- "routes" must be a subset of {"healthcare", "legal", "finance"}.
- "sub_questions" must contain exactly one entry per element of "routes" (and no extras).
- If "routes" is empty, "sub_questions" must be {}.
- "requires_recency_disclosure" must always be present (true or false).
- "recency_notes" must be a string; empty when requires_recency_disclosure is false.
